reason: Vitamin salad is associated with Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian everyday Soviet-derived cooking; these modern associations fit the vegetable, apple and sour-cream salad rather than treating the former USSR as a current country.
Provençal-style sauerkraut with berries is a Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian cold salad tradition; its name does not establish French origin.
Darnitsa rye-wheat bread has established Russian and Ukrainian associations, both already present in the original entry; retain both modern countries.

The Soviet-style plombir ice-cream sandwich remains associated with Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian ice-cream traditions; these are modern dish associations, not a mechanical list of former republics.
Altai honey is a regional Russian food product; the Altai association supports Russia rather than a historical Soviet code.
Squash caviar is an established preserved vegetable spread in Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian cooking, with those common modern associations replacing the historical-only code.
Makarony po-flotski is explicitly described as Russian and is also a familiar Ukrainian and Belarusian pasta-and-minced-meat dish in shared Soviet-derived cuisine.
The original entry explicitly identifies Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian cuisines for this layered fish-and-egg salad; retain all three modern associations.

Morkovcha is a Koryo-saram carrot salad tied to Korean diaspora cooking in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan and to Russian and Ukrainian food traditions; Korean ethnicity does not by itself make it a traditional dish of either Korean state.
Snezhok is the specifically Russian sweet cultured-milk preparation; the original Soviet code is replaced with its modern Russian culinary association rather than all former Soviet countries.
Ketwurst is explicitly an East German hot dog; its continuing modern country association is Germany.
Schwedeneisbecher is an East German ice-cream sundae tradition; its modern country association is Germany, and its Swedish name does not establish Swedish cuisine.
